newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Tedco in three-for-one share split.
newsitem.headline: Tedco in three-for-one share split.

text.p: Zimbabwean clothing and furniture retailer Tedco Ltd on Thursday announced a three-for-one share split of its ordinary shares.
The split increases the number of shares to 240 million worth 10 cents each, from 60 million shares worth 40 cents each.

Tedco secretary Roy Ellis said that the company stock had become too expensive for the small investor on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange and the share split would make the share more marketable and help move the price up.
"The share price had got rather high so we thought we should split the share... It makes a more attractive proposition and keeps shares moving," Ellis told Reuters.

Tedco's share price reached a peak of 1,280 cents per share on January 10 as investors savoured forecasts of firm economic growth in 1997 on the back of good rains, falling annual inflation and lower interest rates.
It has since retraced, closing Wednesday's session at 1,125 cents per share.
Following the share split, the company's authorised share capital increases to Z$27 million from Z$24 million.
The new shares will be listed on March 24.
